scheme_name: National Organic Farming Research Institute (NOFRI) Certification
overview: The National Organic Farming Research Institute (NOFRI) Certification scheme, based at https://nofri.org.in, provides organic certification services for agricultural producers and processors. It operates under the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and focuses on verifying compliance with national organic standards. The institute supports the growth of organic farming through technical guidance, training, and certification for domestic and export markets.
objectives: To provide organic certification in accordance with National Programme for Organic Production (NPOP) standards
To facilitate market access for organic produce domestically and internationally
To offer technical support and training in organic farming practices
To strengthen the organic agriculture value chain through quality assurance
eligibility: Farmers, producer groups, processors, traders, and exporters engaged in organic agriculture or processing who wish to certify their products under NPOP standards are eligible to apply for certification through NOFRI.
benefits: Certification enables access to premium organic markets, eligibility for export under NPOP, consumer trust through recognized quality label, and compliance with domestic and international organic regulations. Certified entities can use the 'India Organic' logo on their products.
financial_support: NOFRI Certification does not provide direct financial support such as grants, loans, or subsidies. It is a fee-based certification service where applicants pay forfeit costs as per the fee structure defined by the institute based on farm size, processing unit capacity, and scope of certification.
application_process:
1. Submit application form available on NOFRI website or through regional centers
2. Provide farm/unit details including land records, input usage, and processing facilities
3. Undergo initial review of application and documents
4. Schedule and undergo on-site inspection by NOFRI-certified inspectors
5. Submit inspection report for review by certification committee
6. Receive certification decision; if approved, issuance of certificate valid for one year
7. Undergo annual surveillance and renewal inspection for continued certification
required_documents: Previous year's production and sales records
Affidavit regarding non-use of prohibited substances
Identity and address proof of applicant
deadlines: Applications are accepted throughout the year on a rolling basis; there is no fixed annual deadline.
implementing_agency: National Organic Farming Research Institute (NOFRI), Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
caveats: Certification is valid for one year and requires annual renewal
Applicants must bear all inspection and certification costs
Failure to comply with NPOP standards during surveillance may lead to suspension or cancellation
The 'India Organic' logo can only be used on certified products
